title: Delivery-failure webhook replay defeats the one-cycle exhaustion gate: a stale/duplicate bounce of the pre-correction send terminalizes the corrected row as unreachable and stamps a false referee_contact_invalid fraud signal
evidence: webhooks.gleam:89-90 documents the assumed dedup: "The svix message id is the idempotency key (svix re-delivers with the same id on retry)" — but `event_id` is never stored or compared; it is used only in a Sentry capture (webhooks.gleam:351). The actual dedup is purely status-scoped: find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql:34-36 matches `WHERE rc.status IN ('queued','contact_initiated') AND (rc.attempts @> NULLIF($1,'')::jsonb OR ...)`, and the attempts log is append-only (`attempts = attempts || $2::jsonb`, sweep_claim_t0.sql:25 / append_reference_call_attempt.sql:5), so the pre-correction `delivered` entry for the OLD message id persists after correction. The RC4.3 branch at webhooks.gleam:285-295 then routes any matched event on a live row to `exhaust_row` whenever `row.correction_cycles >= 1`, and exhaust_reference_call.sql:29's guard (`status IN ('queued','contact_initiated')`) passes because the corrected row is live again. Timeline: first bounce -> awaiting_correction (cycles=0; a redelivery here no-ops because the row is not live) -> landlord corrects -> queued (cycles=1, correct_reference_call.sql leaves attempts untouched) -> sweep re-sends -> contact_initiated. A svix redelivery of the ORIGINAL bounce (the at-least-once behavior the code itself documents at webhooks.gleam:89), or a second distinct actionable event for the same message (resend_terminal_reason maps three event types to reasons: email.bounced / email.complained / email.failed, webhooks.gleam:466-470), now resolves the row again via the persisted delivered entry and is treated as the SECOND failure: the row is terminalized to unreachable and stamp_referee_contact_invalid.sql sets `fraud_signals.referee_contact_invalid = true`. Pre-RC4.3 the same replay was a benign no-op (while awaiting) or a recoverable re-await (after re-queuing); RC4.3 escalates it to a terminal state plus a fraud signal the SQL comments explicitly claim is never fabricated ("rc3-7 never fabricates the signal" — exhaust_reference_call.sql / stamp_referee_contact_invalid.sql).
analysis: AD-7's exhaustion semantics require the SECOND failure to be a failure of the corrected contact's NEW send. The implementation cannot distinguish that from a replay of the first failure's event, because the idempotency key (svix message id) is never persisted and the dedup window (live status) re-opens at the moment of correction. A genuine duplicate delivery (documented at-least-once redelivery, or bounce+failed+complaint variants for one message) therefore satisfies `correction_cycles >= 1` and the status guard, producing: (1) a false `unreachable` terminal on a row the landlord just corrected and that has a fresh invite in flight (the correction is effectively undone and the fresh invite's eventual success would be a late-completion corner), and (2) a false `referee_contact_invalid` fraud signal written into fraud_signals, which feeds the fraud lens (rc3-7) and the AI scoring surface — a fabricated signal on a legitimate referee, in a compliance-relevant (GDPR / EU AI Act) product. The webhook signature gates (svix / Twilio HMAC) are correctly verified, so this is not attacker-forgeable, but provider-normal event duplication is enough to trigger it; the window is open from the correction until the next terminal event. This is a real defect of the new exhaustion mechanism introduced by this PR, not a phantom edge: the code's own comments assert the redelivery behavior that defeats it.
recommendation: Make the exhaustion gate key on the row's CURRENT send rather than any historical one: match the send-ref against the LATEST delivered entry in the attempts log (e.g. compare against `attempts->-1`/last-element `detail`), or persist processed (event_id / send_ref) pairs so a replayed event is a true no-op across the awaiting->queued cycle. At minimum, gate `exhaust_row` on the matched send being the row's most recent send and add an integration test: bounce -> awaiting_correction -> correct -> re-send -> redeliver the FIRST bounce -> assert the row is still live (queued/contact_initiated), not unreachable, and fraud_signals does not carry referee_contact_invalid.
